match.reason: The brief combines two ideas, charities such as the Red Cross and government foreign aid for health, water and education, and neither bank point covers both: the NGO point covers only non-government groups and the overseas aid point covers only government aid, so a single match would teach only half of it.

draft.title: Non-government organisations and aid
card: A non-government organisation (NGO) is a group that is not run by a government. Many are charities that raise money from donations. The Red Cross is one example.
Foreign aid is help that one country's government gives to another country. It can be money, goods or skills. Australia gives foreign aid to countries in the Pacific and Asia.
NGOs and foreign aid both fund projects that can improve wellbeing. These include clinics and vaccines for health, wells and pipes for clean water, and schools and teacher training for education.
The difference is the giver. An NGO is a private group. Foreign aid comes from a government, often paid for by its taxpayers.
draft.remember: NGOs are groups outside government. Foreign aid is a government helping another country.

a.q: Which of these is an example of foreign aid?
opts: The Australian Government funds a water project in Fiji
A charity runs a school lunch program using donations
A local council builds a new park in its own town
A state government opens a new hospital in Sydney
a.why: Foreign aid is help from one country's government to another country. The charity is an NGO, not a government. The council and state hospital help people inside Australia, so they are not foreign aid.
a.clue: Look for a government helping people in another country.

b.q: A charity in Sydney raises money from public donations. It uses the money to pay for vaccines in a village in Kenya. How is the charity best described?
opts: An NGO, because it is not run by a government
Foreign aid, because the money goes to another country
A government initiative, because it improves health
Foreign aid, because it helps people in need
b.why: The charity is not run by a government, so it is an NGO. Sending help overseas does not make it foreign aid, because foreign aid comes from a government. Improving health is a goal that NGOs and governments share.
b.clue: Ask who runs the charity, not where the help goes.

a.best: The Australian Government funds a water project in Fiji

b.best: An NGO, because it is not run by a government
